title: Small-business credit is a differentiated route shaped by lender choice and firm risk
source_unit: Federal Reserve Small Business Credit Survey 2023 small employer-firm applicants, as summarized in Consumer & Community Context

denominator.unit: small employer firms in the SBCS survey population

credit_application_rate.unit: percent applying for loan, line of credit, or merchant cash advance in prior 12 months

observations.method: Federal Reserve summary of the Small Business Credit Survey; application rate uses small employer firms, while provider shares use applicant firms.
observations.uncertainty: Application and provider-choice estimates come from a survey and use different denominators; the source does not establish why firms chose providers or whether applications were simultaneous.
observations.subgroup: Small employer firms and small employer-firm credit applicants.
observations.counterinterpretation: Provider shares reflect firm needs, product fit, speed, risk, and applicant composition, not a universal lender preference or quality ranking.

observations.period: 2023; loan, line-of-credit, and cash-advance applicants by reported credit risk

denominator.unit: applicant firms within lender and risk cells

observations.method: Federal Reserve summary comparing approval rates by lender type and self-reported low versus medium/high credit-risk category.
observations.uncertainty: Risk and lender cells are observational survey comparisons; applicant pools, requested amounts, products, and underwriting standards differ.
observations.subgroup: Small employer-firm applicants by reported credit-risk category and lender type.
observations.counterinterpretation: Risk-patterned approval differences may reflect legitimate underwriting, collateral, credit history, product fit, or amount requested; they are not a causal lender-effect estimate.

observations.period: 2023; small employer-firm applicants by lender type

denominator.unit: applicant firms within each lender-type cell

observations.method: Federal Reserve summary of at-least-partial and full approval rates across lender categories; comparison includes other nonbank finance companies, credit unions, and CDFIs in the published figure.
observations.uncertainty: Provider cells have different firms, products, requested amounts, and selection processes; partial approval is not the same as receiving the requested amount.
observations.subgroup: Small employer-firm credit applicants by lender category.
observations.counterinterpretation: A lower full-approval share may accompany faster access, different risk, smaller product fit, or a different requested amount; rates do not rank lender welfare or firm outcomes.

boundary: This record establishes application, provider-choice, and approval differences for small employer-firm credit applicants. It does not establish funding receipt, terms, repayment, firm investment, survival, jobs, owner-household effects, local spillovers, or causal provider quality.
